study_schedule.source_excerpt: Study Duration; Study Schedule of Events and Visit Descriptions: "Study Duration The duration of the study for each patient is approximately 28 weeks, excluding" "postponed until this requirement is met, but without exceeding the 35-day maximum" "duration for screening." "During the treatment period, patients will have weekly in-clinic visits through week 4, and then" "in-clinic visits every 4 weeks through week 16 with weekly telephone visits in between the" "in-clinic visits." "treatment period visit will occur at week 16, two weeks after the last dose of study drug." "Patients who decline to enroll in the open-label extension study will be followed up for" "12 weeks." "For these patients, after week 16, follow-up visits will occur every 4 weeks from" "week 20 through week 28." "Table 2: Schedule of Events (Treatment Period cont, Follow-Up Period, Unscheduled Visits, and Early Termination)" "In-clinic Visit (V) PV15a PV16a PV17a V18 V19 V20 V21" "Week (W) W13 W14 W15 W16 W20 W24 W28" "Study Day (D) D92 D99 D106 D113 D141 D169 D197" "200 mg Q2W from week 2 to week 14, or" "300 mg Q2W from week 2 to week 14" "patient) will be trained on injecting study drug during in-clinic visit 2 (day 1) to visit 6 (week 4)." "In-clinic Visit (V) or Phone V1 V2 V3 V4 V5 V6 PV7a PV8a PV9a V10 PV11a PV12a PV13a V14" "Week (W) W1 W2 W3 W4 W5 W6 W7 W8 W9 W10 W11 W12" "The site will contact the patient/caregiver by telephone to conduct these visits." "In-clinic Visit (V) or Phone V1 V2 V3 V4 V5 V6 PV7a PV8a PV9a V10 PV11a PV12a PV13a V14" "Week (W) W1 W2 W3 W4 W5 W6 W7 W8 W9 W10 W11 W12" "In-clinic Visit (V) PV15a PV16a PV17a V18 V19 V20 V21" "Week (W) W13 W14 W15 W16 W20 W24 W28" "treatment, the patients will be encouraged to stay in the study to have data collected at all" "remaining scheduled visits until completion of the planned end of study visit." -- Screening is allowed up to 35 days. Baseline/day 1 begins randomized treatment (represented without assigning week 0); treatment has weekly clinic visits through week 4 and every-four-week clinic visits through week 16, with weekly phone contacts between them. Visit-week values 1–4 and 8, 12, 16 come from the protocol schedule cadence and W1–W16 table labels; follow-up clinic weeks 20, 24, and 28 are the W20/W24/W28 table labels, with exact four-week intervals. The week 5–15 phone-contact integer list is left null because the protocol states only weekly telephone visits between clinic visits. The last dose is at week 14 and end of treatment is week 16, two weeks later. The approximately 28-week duration excludes screening; follow-up applies to those who decline the OLE.

value.rationale: Rescue for intolerable atopic dermatitis symptoms may be provided at investigator discretion. If possible, the protocol encourages starting with topical treatment and escalating to systemic medication only after inadequate response to at least 7 days of topical treatment. Topical rescue may be given while study treatment continues; systemic corticosteroid or systemic nonsteroidal immunosuppressive rescue requires permanent study-drug discontinuation. Participants are asked to complete scheduled visits and assessments regardless of treatment completion or rescue use; participants who prematurely discontinue study treatment are encouraged to remain through the planned end-of-study visit. The protocol specifies week 28 as the end-of-study visit for participants declining the open-label extension, so 28 is the follow-through horizon for that non-extension schedule, not a universal visit commitment for participants entering the extension. Rescue use is considered treatment failure for efficacy analysis.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Protocol Sections 3.1, 5.3, and 5.4.2; planned follow-up schedule: "If patients prematurely discontinue study" "treatment, the patients will be encouraged to stay in the study to have data collected at all" "remaining scheduled visits until completion of the planned end of study visit." "Patients who decline to enroll in the open-label extension study will be followed up for" "12 weeks." "For these patients, after week 16, follow-up visits will occur every 4 weeks from" "week 20 through week 28." "If medically necessary (ie, to control intolerable AD symptoms), rescue treatment for AD may be" "provided to study patients at the discretion of the investigator." "encouraged to consider rescue initially with topical treatment (eg, medium/high potency TCS)" "and to escalate to systemic medications only for patients who do not respond adequately after at" "least 7 days of topical treatment." "Topical calcineurin inhibitors may be used for rescue, alone or" "in combination with TCS, but the use of TCIs should be reserved for problem areas only (eg," "face, neck, intertriginous and genital areas, etc.)." "Investigators may also consider rescue with" "crisaborole." "Patients may continue study treatment if rescue consists of" "topical medications." "Patients who receive systemic corticosteroids or systemic nonsteroidal immunosuppressive drugs" "(eg, cyclosporine, methotrexate, mycophenolate-mofetil, azathioprine, etc) as rescue medication" "during the study will be discontinued permanently from the study drug." "to complete the scheduled study visits and assessments whether or not they complete study" "treatment and whether or not they receive rescue treatment for AD." "For the purpose of efficacy analysis, patients who" "receive rescue treatment during the study will be considered treatment failures." "Patients who permanently discontinue from study drug and who do not withdraw from the study" "will be asked to return to the clinic for all remaining study visits per the visit schedule." -- continue_visits_through_week is week 28 for the non-extension schedule: protocol Section 3.1 states visits through week 28 for patients declining OLE and encourages early treatment discontinuers to remain through the planned end-of-study visit; Sections 5.3 and 5.4.2 require continued scheduled follow-up after rescue or study-drug discontinuation. This does not imply that extension participants have a week-28 end of study.

published_results.source_excerpt: 14.1 Atopic Dermatitis; Table 20: "Figure 1 Pediatric Subjects 12 Years of Age and Older with Atopic Dermatitis The efficacy of DUPIXENT monotherapy in pediatric subjects 12 years of age and older was evaluated in a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AD-1526; NCT03054428) in 251 pediatric subjects 12 to 17 years of age, with moderate-to-severe AD defined by an IGA score ≥3 (scale of 0 to 4), an EASI score ≥16 (scale of 0 to 72), and a minimum BSA involvement of ≥10%." "Subjects in the DUPIXENT group with baseline weight of <60 kg received an initial dose of 400 mg at Week 0, followed by 200 mg Q2W for 16 weeks." "Subjects with baseline weight of ≥60 kg received an initial dose of 600 mg at Week 0, followed by 300 mg Q2W for 16 weeks." "The primary endpoint was the proportion of subjects with an IGA 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) and at least a 2-point improvement from baseline to Week 16." "The efficacy results at Week 16 for AD-1526 are presented in Table 20." "Table 20: Efficacy Results of DUPIXENT in AD-1526 at Week 16 (FAS) Full Analysis Set (FAS) includes all subjects randomized." "in Pediatric Subjects 12 Years of Age and Older with Moderate-to-Severe AD DUPIXENT At Week 0, subjects received 400 mg (baseline weight <60 kg) or 600 mg (baseline weight ≥60 kg) of DUPIXENT." "200 mg (<60 kg) or 300 mg (≥60 kg) Q2W N=82 Placebo N=85 IGA 0 or 1 Responder was defined as a subject with an IGA 0 or 1 (" ") and a reduction of ≥2 points on a 0-4 IGA scale." "24% 2% EASI-75 42% 8% EASI-90 23% 2% Peak Pruritus NRS (≥4-point improvement) 37% 5% A greater proportion of subjects randomized to DUPIXENT achieved an improvement in the Peak Pruritus NRS compared to placebo (defined as ≥4-point improvement at Week 4)." -- Table 20 reports the AD-1526 Week 16 full analysis set. It presents the Q2W dupilumab arm (N=82) and placebo (N=85); only those label rows are joined to the two matching listed primary endpoint keys. The Week 16 results follow 16 weeks of treatment.
